# BAD-095 — Admin /scenes: an all-time First imported column, plus the column order and default sort Eric asked for

## Brief
Eric, 2026-09-16: "In the admin page under scenes, add a column that shows First Imported so I could see what the oldest most active scenes are." Plus a column order and a new default sort, both spelled out below.

## The column order he asked for

| # | Header | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Scene | `title` (unchanged) |
| 2 | Imported | `libraries` (unchanged) |
| 3 | **First Imported** | **new** |
| 4 | Last Imported | `last_imported_at` (unchanged) |
| 5 | Users Recorded | `users_recorded` (unchanged) |
| 6 | Sessions | `sessions` (unchanged) |
| 7 | Last Recorded | `last_recorded_at` — **the new default sort, descending (newest first)** |

Today's default sort is `sessions` desc, set in two places that must agree: `listScenes`'s `const sortKey: SceneSortKey = isSceneSortKey(query.sort) ? query.sort : 'sessions'` in admin/src/lib/scenes.ts, and the page's own fallback in admin/src/app/scenes/page.tsx. Change both to `last_recorded`. A default that disagrees between them is a page whose header arrow points at one column while the rows are ordered by another.

Keep every existing header's capitalisation convention — the page writes "Users recorded" and "Last imported", sentence case. Eric's list above is his shorthand, not a restyling: render the new one as "First imported" to match its neighbours.

## The decision this ticket turns on

**First imported is all-time. It is not windowed, and a windowed version answers nothing.**

Every column on /scenes today is inside the `?days=` window — `admin/src/lib/scenes.ts`'s header comment states it as an invariant ("both CTEs filter on `created_at >= now() - $1 days` before anything is aggregated, so narrowing the window moves these dates rather than revealing older ones"), and `ACQUIRED_CTE` and `RECORDED_CTE` both carry that filter.

A `min(created_at)` taken over the windowed `acquired` CTE would be the oldest acquisition *inside the window*: on the default 30-day view it can never be older than 30 days, so every scene in the library would report a first import inside the last month and the column would rank nothing. Eric asked for this column to find "the oldest most active scenes". A windowed minimum cannot answer that question, and — this is why the reviewer exists — on a production 30-day view with recent traffic it would look entirely plausible in a screenshot.

So: a **new CTE that reads both acquisition sources with no `created_at` predicate at all**, grouped by the same `lower(btrim(scene_title))` key, producing `min(created_at) as first_imported_at`, left-joined onto `scenes`. The two source halves are the same two `ACQUIRED_CTE` unions: `private.scene_imports` (any `how`) and `private.scene_saves where kind = 'create'`. Same key expression, same `scene_title is not null and btrim(scene_title) <> ''` guard — a different key expression here would join to nothing for any title with stray whitespace, and the column would be a dash on rows that have a date.

Do not reuse `ACQUIRED_CTE` by parameterising its window; write the unwindowed one as its own module constant beside it and say in a comment why there are now two. A shared fragment that takes a flag is a fragment somebody widens the windowed half with by accident, which is the failure the existing header comment is already guarding against.

**This breaks the page's stated invariant, deliberately, and the documentation must say so.** Update the "the timestamps" section of scenes.ts's header comment: it currently promises every date on the page is inside the window, and after this change exactly one is not. Say which, and say why (the column exists to rank scenes by age, and age does not fit in a window). Whoever reads that comment next must not be able to conclude the unwindowed CTE is a bug.

**A consequence the UI has to survive, and should explain in a comment:** a scene first imported two years ago and untouched since shows a real date under First imported and an em dash under both Imported and Last imported on a 30-day window. That is correct and it is the point of the column. Nothing about it should be coalesced or hidden.

`first_imported_at` is nullable in principle (a scene that reached the page only through `recorded` — recorded but never imported by anyone, ever), so render it through the same `TimeAgo` / `relative` / em-dash treatment the two existing dates use, and type it `string | null` on `SceneRow`. Give it a `SORTS` entry so its header sorts; `nulls last` is already appended by the order clause.

## Performance — read admin/CLAUDE.md before you write the query

The dashboard has a documented history of exactly the failure this change risks. `admin/src/lib/db.ts` pools **three** connections, a render that asks for more wedges until Cloud Run kills it at 300s, and `test/server/admin-pool.test.mjs` fails the build if any file under `admin/src` starts concurrent promises. Migrations 0010 and 0011 added bare `(created_at desc)` indexes to these tables precisely because whole-table time windows were sequentially scanning and returning 504s in production on 2026-08-20.

An unwindowed `min(created_at) group by lower(btrim(scene_title))` over the whole of `scene_imports` and `scene_saves` is a full scan of both, and **no `(created_at desc)` index helps it** — there is no index on the key expression. It also cannot be restricted to the page's 50 rows, because sorting by First imported has to order the whole result set before paging.

What is required of you:
- It stays **one round trip**. The new CTE composes into the existing `with` clause of both `listScenes` and `countScenes`; it does not become a second `sql.unsafe` and it does not become a `Promise.all`. The existing test asserts the one-round-trip rule and it must keep passing.
- Reason about the cost against the real table sizes and **write what you found into the comment**. If both tables are small enough that the scan is uninteresting, say so with the number you based it on. If they are not, an index on `lower(btrim(scene_title))` is the fix — but that is a SQL migration, which is the `server-changes` skill and deploys from CI, and it is **out of scope for this ticket**: file it with `spud --as <your id> proposal file` rather than widening this one. Do not write a migration here.
- Never add a second concurrent query to work around it.

## The tests

`test/server/admin-scenes-list.test.mjs` is text assertions over the dashboard's own source; its head comment says plainly what it does and does not prove (it does not prove the SQL is valid or runs). Read that comment first — it is the record of why the file is shaped this way.

Two of its existing tests fail on this change by design and must be updated rather than deleted: `the empty row spans every column the header declares` asserts `headers === 6`, and the colSpan must follow it to 7.

Add, in the shape of what is there:
- `first_imported` names a column the query actually selects, the same guard the two existing sort keys get — an `order by` on a column no CTE produced is a 500 on the first header click, not a build error.
- The first-import aggregate is a `min` over the **unwindowed** CTE. Assert both halves: that it is `min(created_at)`, and that the CTE it sits in carries **no** `created_at >= now()` predicate. A test that only checks for `min(...)` passes against the windowed version, which is the exact mistake this ticket exists to prevent.
- `listScenes` carries `firstImportedAt` onto the row through `iso()`, and `SceneRow` declares it `string | null`.
- The header order is Eric's. Assert the seven `<Th>` headers appear in the given sequence in the source, not merely that each exists — the whole visible half of this ticket is the order.
- The default sort is `last_recorded` in **both** places, and they agree.
- The one-round-trip assertion still holds (it is already written; make sure your change does not make it vacuous).
